title: CQRS & Event Sourcing in .NET
description: Implement CQRS with separated read/write models and Event Sourcing for immutable, auditable domain state.

data.text: Command Query Responsibility Segregation (CQRS) separates the read model from the write model. Commands (writes) encapsulate business logic and produce side effects. Queries (reads) return data without side effects. This separation allows each model to be optimized independently — the write model enforces invariants, while the read model can use denormalized, pre-computed views optimized for query performance.

data.caption: CQRS separates commands (writes) from queries (reads) through distinct models

data.text: Event Sourcing: The Source of Truth

Event Sourcing persists the state of a domain object as a sequence of events rather than as a current snapshot. The current state is reconstructed by replaying events. This provides a complete audit trail, enables temporal queries (what did the state look like at any point in time), and supports replaying events to recover from bugs.

data.text: After a command handler commits domain events, projection handlers update denormalized read models. This can be synchronous (same transaction) or asynchronous (event-driven eventual consistency). For AI applications, read models often pre-compute embeddings or aggregate statistics for fast retrieval.

rows: Separate read DB, eventual consistency OK

data.text: Event Sourcing introduces complexity: event versioning, snapshotting for long-lived aggregates, handling schema changes, and debugging event streams. Use it only for domains where auditability, temporal queries, or high write throughput justify the cost.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: CQRS separates commands (business logic) from queries (data retrieval)
Event Sourcing persists state as immutable event streams instead of current snapshots
Projections build read models from domain events for optimized querying
MediatR with pipeline behaviors provides clean cross-cutting concern handling
Use idempotency and the Outbox pattern for reliable async event processing
data.takeaway: CQRS + Event Sourcing enables auditable, scalable write models paired with optimized read models, but adds complexity that pays off in domains requiring traceability and temporal queries.
